title: An old invoice reversed and invoiced again sends the new text to QuickBooks
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a test location whose QuickBooks Online connection is active, linked to a QuickBooks sandbox company you can sign in to.
  • Have a work order made before this release, work order 1, for customer A, invoiced and synced to QuickBooks before this release as invoice A, with a labor line, line 1, that has a title, a description and a tech story.
  • Write down line 1's title, description and tech story.
  • Keep the QuickBooks sandbox company open in a second browser tab.
  • Start on work order 1, on its Finance tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click invoice A's three-dot menu.
  2. Click Reverse.
  3. Click Reverse in the confirmation.
  4. Click Create Invoice.
  5. Close the New Customer Payment window without taking a payment.
  6. In the QuickBooks tab, search for customer A's invoices.
  7. Open the newest invoice for customer A.
  8. Open invoice A.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens with Reverse.

Step 2:

  • A confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • Invoice A is reversed and Create Invoice is offered again on work order 1.

Step 4:

  • A new invoice for work order 1 is created.

Step 5:

  • The payment window closes.

Step 6:

  • QuickBooks lists invoice A and the new invoice for customer A.

Step 7:

  • The new invoice's line 1 Description reads line 1's title, " - ", its description, " - " and its tech story, as written down, with no field names and no semicolon.

Step 8:

  • Invoice A's line 1 Description still reads in the old form, starting "What are you doing?:": both forms now sit in the same books for one job.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 15 (14 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks)

  • S3-E2: “An invoice that is reversed and re-invoiced after release day carries the new text on the new invoice, while the original keeps the old text. A bookkeeper can therefore see both forms in one set of books, on one job.”
  • S3-N1: “Invoices already in QuickBooks keep the text they were sent with. Nothing is re-synced to QuickBooks or rewritten there.”
  • Key Decisions: “Nothing already in QuickBooks changes. No backfill, no re-send, no re-export. The new text applies to invoices synced or exported from release day onward. A reversal produces a new invoice, so it carries the new text, which means an invoice and its reversal can read differently in the same books. Accepted deliberately.”

Not yet checked against a build by us: the QA build (sv10130.qa.shopview.com, QuickBooks host qb1.qa.shopview.com) and staging carry this change, and this case has not been run on either.
